prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, the injuries, whether the other driver was uninsured, whether a governmental defendant is involved, and your personal preferences (price, communication style, willingness to go to trial).

How to find the best attorney for your case
- Experience and track record: look for attorneys who focus on automobile collisions and who have secured sizeable settlements or jury verdicts for similar injuries.
- Trial experience: if fault or damages are disputed, you want someone who will try the case if necessary (not just settle).
- Resources and staff: serious cases may require accident reconstruction, medical experts, and investigators.
- Communication and responsiveness: ask how often you’ll get updates and who you’ll talk to.
- Reputation and discipline history: check peer reviews (Martindale‑Hubbell), Super Lawyers lists, Avvo ratings, Google/BBB reviews, and state bar records.
- Fee arrangement and costs: most Chicago PI attorneys work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm the percentage, when costs are deducted, and whether the rate changes if the case goes to trial.

Practical items to know right away
- Statute of limitations: in Illinois most personal injury claims must be filed within two years of the accident (there are exceptions). Don’t wait to consult an attorney.
- Typical contingency fees: commonly 25–40% of recovery; exact percentages and cost handling vary — get it in writing.
- Free consultation: many firms offer a free case review — use that to compare options.

Where to look for top attorneys
- Super Lawyers (Chicago — Personal Injury)
- Martindale‑Hubbell peer reviews
- Avvo and Google Reviews
- Illinois State Bar Association referral service

If you want, I can:
- Build a short list (3–5) of highly rated Chicago car-accident attorneys/firms with recent notable settlements/verdicts and contact info, or
- Suggest the questions to ask during an initial consultation and a checklist of documents to bring.

Tell me (briefly): what neighborhood in Chicago or zip code you prefer, when the accident happened, and whether the injuries are serious — I’ll prepare a tailored shortlist.
